issue.issue_text: Whether the respondents employed in the electricity department of the Baroda Municipality were entitled to the bonus claimed.

facts: The respondents were employees in the electricity department of the Baroda Municipality.
The Industrial Tribunal initially decided that the employees were not entitled to the bonus.
The Labour Appellate Tribunal overturned the Industrial Tribunal's decision, finding that the employees were entitled to the bonus.
law: The text does not specify the legal principles or statutes used by the court, as it only contains the concluding paragraph of the judgment, which refers to "reasons given above" that are not included in the provided text.
application: The Supreme Court reviewed the decisions of the lower tribunals.
It found that the Industrial Tribunal had reached the correct decision in denying the bonus.
Conversely, the court determined that the Labour Appellate Tribunal had made an "erroneous decision" in granting the bonus.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court held that the employees of the electricity department of the Baroda Municipality were not entitled to the bonus they claimed. Consequently, the court allowed the appeal and set aside the order of the Labour Appellate Tribunal.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The authority of the government to make a declaration under the proviso to Section 8(1) of the Jammu and Kashmir Preventive Detention Act, stating that it is against the public interest to communicate the grounds of detention, must be exercised within the same time limit prescribed for communicating the grounds themselves, which is "as soon as may be". The time for making the declaration is co-terminous with the time for communicating the grounds. Failure to make such a declaration within this period renders the detention illegal.
obiter: Section 14 of the Jammu and Kashmir Preventive Detention Act does not in terms provide for the making of a formal order and there is no scope for the contention that the decision of the Government thereunder that a detention order should be continued must be communicated to the detenue concerned within three months of his detention.
